expected_alphas_derivation_methodology.definition: expected_alphas (per ticker) = the sorted union of acceptable_alphas across every ALPHA_HIT / COMPOSITE_STRUCTURE_HIT / CONDITIONAL_ACCEPTANCE_HIT rule for that ticker whose frozen_trigger_state (as already adjudicated in Step 3 and recorded per-rule in the frozen v0_2_final_acceptance_table.json) is exactly 'PRESENT'. NEGATIVE_CONTROL_HIT rules are excluded from expected_alphas -- their acceptable_alphas field names a forbidden-dominant target, not an expected-detection target, and are instead used to derive forbidden_dominant_alphas.
expected_alphas_derivation_methodology.why_not_a_naive_union_of_all_acceptable_: A naive union across every rule regardless of trigger state would silently resurrect exactly the fixed-mandatory-Alpha-set model Gold v0.2 explicitly retired (see gold_authority.model_note), and would contradict the frozen v0_2_final_acceptance_table.json's own anti_leakage.expected_alpha_set_model_used=false flag. Filtering to PRESENT-trigger rules only preserves the evidence-conditional model: an Alpha is only 'expected' when its own defining evidence condition was independently confirmed present before any run result was inspected.
expected_alphas_derivation_methodology.uncertain_trigger_alphas_excluded: Rules whose frozen_trigger_state is UNCERTAIN (e.g. QQQ-A003, QQQ-ETF-CONTEXT-CONTROL, MSFT-A102-INDIRECT-INFERENCE-SUPPORT) are excluded from expected_alphas (evidence not confirmed present) but are never silently dropped -- each appears in per-ticker notes.
expected_alphas_derivation_methodology.expected_dominant_alphas_definition: Gold v0.2's rule_type_semantics defines no 'must be dominant' rule type at all -- only 'forbidden_dominant_without_strong_evidence' (a negative constraint). Therefore expected_dominant_alphas = [] for every ticker, by design, not by omission. unexpected_dominant_alphas is instead computed as (actual_dominant_alphas intersect forbidden_dominant_alphas) -- i.e. a genuine forbidden-dominance violation.
expected_alphas_derivation_methodology.main_conflict_match_definition: true iff (actual_main_conflict is null AND allowed_main_conflicts is empty) [no conflict occurred, none was required -- a legitimate, non-violating state] OR (actual_main_conflict is a member of allowed_main_conflicts). false iff an actual_main_conflict exists that is not in a non-applicable/empty allowed list, OR an actual_main_conflict exists that is outside a non-empty allowed list. This distinguishes MSFT/SNDK's legitimate 'no conflict, none required' outcome from QQQ/TSM's 'an unaddressed real conflict emerged' outcome -- both are still fully adjudicated in conflict_mismatch_adjudication below regardless of the boolean's value.
expected_alphas_derivation_methodology.reused_not_recomputed: All frozen_trigger_state, acceptable_alphas, allowed_main_conflicts, forbidden_dominant_alphas, actual_detected_alphas, actual_dominant_alphas, and actual_main_conflict values are read directly, unmodified, from the frozen docs/audit_artifacts/v0_2_final_acceptance_table.json and docs/audit_artifacts/v0_2_gold_operational_contract.json -- none was recomputed from raw run artifacts, since the frozen tables already contain the full per-rule actual_alpha_states from the same six persisted runs.

conflict_evaluation_semantics.verification_method: Directly inspected every rule's hit_type, rule_type, and allowed_main_conflicts field across all 19 frozen Gold v0.2 rules in v0_2_gold_operational_contract.json (SHA256 e2df7139e19ec998afc6335caf4d53528dd3f4356a46d4e9a88d9d04b520000f, unmodified), plus the contract's own rule_type_semantics dictionary, which is the sole authoritative definition of what each rule_type -- including allowed_main_conflicts -- means. Not inferred from field emptiness alone.
conflict_evaluation_semantics.verified_finding: rule_type_semantics.allowed_main_conflicts reads (verbatim): 'One or more existing canonical conflict structures may satisfy the Gold thesis when both sides are currently supported. No conflict is forced when one side lacks sufficient evidence.' This is an AFFIRMATIVE/PERMISSIVE rule type -- it describes what happens when a rule of this type is authored and populated. Gold v0.2's rule_type_semantics dictionary contains NO rule type meaning 'no conflict is allowed' or 'conflicts are forbidden for this ticker' -- the only forbidding rule type that exists at all is forbidden_dominant_without_strong_evidence, which forbids a specific Alpha from being DOMINANT, not a conflict PAIR from being admitted. allowed_main_conflicts=[] appears on every ALPHA_HIT, NEGATIVE_CONTROL_HIT, and CONDITIONAL_ACCEPTANCE_HIT rule across all six tickers (17 of 19 rules total) purely because those rules are not of the allowed_main_conflicts rule_type at all -- the field is a structural placeholder on non-conflict rules, not a declared prohibition. Critically, TSM's own COMPOSITE_STRUCTURE_HIT rule (TSM-AI-TO-FOUNDRY-TRANSMISSION) also carries allowed_main_conflicts=[] -- but its rule_type is 'conditional_only' and its concept is an explicitly supportive transmission chain (A101->A201->A301), never a bull/bear conflict thesis -- proving hit_type=COMPOSITE_STRUCTURE_HIT alone does not imply conflict-family governance either; only a rule actually typed/populated as allowed_main_conflicts does. Exactly 2 of 19 rules (NVDA-GROWTH-VS-VALUATION-CONFLICT, AMD-AI-GROWTH-VS-VALUATION) are populated with real conflict pairs -- these are the only two tickers where Gold v0.2 governs a main-conflict family at all.
conflict_evaluation_semantics.answer: 2. NO CONFLICT RULE WAS AUTHORED / NOT GOVERNED. allowed_main_conflicts=[] does NOT mean 'no conflict is allowed' for QQQ, MSFT, SNDK, or TSM -- it means Gold v0.2 never authored a conflict-family acceptance rule for that ticker at all. Only NVDA and AMD have an explicit, populated allowed_main_conflicts rule and are therefore conflict-governed.
